section_heading: Work while your course is in session
text: Student visa holders may work up to 48 hours in a fortnight while their course is in session. Student visa holders cannot work in Australia before their course starts. Students undertaking a master's degree by research or a doctoral degree, and their family members, are exempt from this limit. A student's own grant conditions should be checked in VEVO because visa conditions can differ.

A work-experience unit that is a mandatory component of a course and is included in the course's CRICOS registration is not counted toward the student visa work limit. Home Affairs gives the example of a mandatory four-week pharmacy placement that is documented in the registered course structure. Placement that is not a mandatory course requirement, or that goes beyond the period required in the course registration, does not fall within this exception. Check the course documentation with the education provider before relying on it.

Student visa condition 8105 limits work to 48 hours a fortnight while the course is in session, and a fortnight is a 14-day period starting on a Monday. Home Affairs counts work experience toward this limit whether it is paid or unpaid. A course is in session during school semesters, including exam periods. Students should add up all hours worked in each fortnight and check their own visa conditions in VEVO.

section_heading: National Minimum Wage and award rates
text: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week before tax for adults whose employment is not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. Casual employees covered by the National Minimum Wage also receive a 25% casual loading. Most employees are covered by an award, which sets minimum rates for particular industries and occupations, and lower rates can apply to juniors. An employee cannot agree to be paid less than the minimum rate that applies to their job. The Fair Work Pay Calculator (PACT) can be used to find the minimum wage under an award.

section_heading: Workplace rights regardless of visa status
text: International students have the same entitlements and protections under the Fair Work Act as other employees, regardless of their migration status under the Migration Act. All employees have basic rights, including minimum pay and conditions. Not being given a pay slip is not okay at work: an employee should receive a pay slip within one day of being paid. A sponsoring employer cannot cancel a visa; only the Department of Home Affairs can grant, refuse or cancel visas.

If an employee believes they are not receiving their minimum pay or other workplace rights, the Fair Work Ombudsman provides free information and advice. It can be contacted through Fair Work Online or the Fair Work Infoline on 13 13 94, and language help is available through the Translating and Interpreting Service on 13 14 50. A migrant worker can still ask the Fair Work Ombudsman for help to get minimum entitlements even if they have breached visa conditions. The Ombudsman says a person cannot get into trouble or have their visa cancelled for contacting it to ask about pay or workplace rights.

section_heading: Check work rights after course completion
text: A Student visa page describes work limits while a course is in session and says students can work unlimited hours when the course is not in session. It does not mean every student automatically has unrestricted work rights after course completion: the person's visa status and conditions matter. Check the visa grant notice and VEVO, and obtain migration advice for individual circumstances. A different visa may be needed for work after a student visa ceases.

section_heading: What OSHC is and how long it applies
text: Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is health insurance for international students living and studying in Australia. It is a visa requirement for most Student visa subclass 500 holders and must be in place for the student's entire stay in Australia. OSHC is not Medicare, and most international students are not eligible for Medicare, so OSHC is how they access healthcare. Check the policy dates against the visa grant and insurer documents so there is no gap in cover.

For a non-emergency illness, Study Melbourne recommends starting with a general practitioner (GP), which is often more affordable than going directly to a hospital. Visiting doctors, specialists or hospitals in the insurer's network can reduce out-of-pocket expenses. If the student pays upfront for a service, they should save the receipts and submit a claim through the insurer's app, email or website to be reimbursed. The amount returned depends on the policy and the service.

Basic OSHC does not include optical care such as glasses, or dental care such as check-ups, fillings or dental surgery. A student can pay an additional premium for Extras cover, which can include dental and optical services. For dental care, Study Australia lists paying privately at a dental clinic, checking whether the OSHC provider offers optional extras cover, or using low-cost local or university dental clinics. Delaying dental care can lead to bigger problems later, so it is a good idea to ask about costs early.

OSHC policies differ, so students should carefully read their policy terms to understand which services are covered and how to use their cover. Optional extras depend on the plan, and some policies include services such as physiotherapy, dental care and optical services. Study Melbourne advises confirming with the insurer what costs are covered before scheduling planned treatment. Using providers in the insurer's network can reduce out-of-pocket expenses.

section_heading: Reciprocal Health Care Agreements for visitors
text: Australia has Reciprocal Health Care Agreements with 11 countries: Belgium, Finland, Italy, Malta, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Ireland, Slovenia, Sweden and the United Kingdom. Visitors from these countries may be eligible for medically necessary care under Medicare while they are in Australia. Eligibility depends on the agreement: the United Kingdom and Belgium pages say student visa holders are eligible, while the Norway page says they are not. Check the Services Australia page for the specific country before relying on an agreement.

section_heading: OSHC remains a Student visa requirement
text: OSHC is a visa requirement for most students on a Student visa subclass 500 and must be in place for the student's entire stay. OSHC is not the same as Medicare, which is Australia's public health insurance for citizens and permanent residents. Students should keep their OSHC policy active and confirm any claimed exception directly with the Department of Home Affairs and their insurer before changing or cancelling cover.

If someone is experiencing a medical emergency or is at immediate risk in Victoria, call Triple Zero (000) or go to a hospital emergency department. Tell the operator whether police, fire or ambulance is needed and give the exact location if possible. Study Melbourne also describes 112 for situations where the phone has no service or is not connected to the network. Do not use an information chatbot in place of emergency services.

In Victoria, the cost of ambulance transport is not covered by Medicare. Ambulance Victoria decides how best to transport a patient, and different fees apply to different kinds of transport. The Department of Health notes that there are several ways patients can insure against the cost of ambulance transport, so students should check whether their own health cover includes it. Cost should never delay a call for help in an emergency.

Tap on at the start of each trip. Tap off at the end on trains, buses that accept myki, and tram trips that begin and end in Zone 2. For a tram trip that starts and ends in Zone 1, tap on but do not tap off. Tap on again when changing transport modes. A green light or phone confirmation indicates the tap registered; failing to tap correctly can mean there is no valid ticket or a default fare applies.

The International Student Travel Pass is a discount program for eligible international students, not a concession automatically given to every international student. Study Melbourne says eligible students can get a 50% discount and save over $1,000. Passes are available for 90, 180 or 365 days, and state-wide passes allow travel across Victoria for the same price as within Melbourne. Eligibility is checked through the public transport website before a pass is bought.

section_heading: Who can buy the International Student Travel Pass
text: Transport Victoria says the International Student Travel Pass is available to students who study full time, are enrolled in a bachelor or associate degree, diploma or advanced diploma, and study at an institution that has signed up to the program. International exchange students, students with refugee status and Australian Award Scholarship recipients follow the local undergraduate student process instead. To apply, ask the institution for a pass code, then register and buy the pass on the program website. Carry the pass when travelling.

section_heading: From Melbourne Airport to the city
text: Study Melbourne lists SkyBus as a frequent connection between Melbourne Airport and Southern Cross Station in the city centre. Other options include taxis, rideshare, public buses and shuttles. Journey time and fares vary, so check the airport or operator's live timetable and price before travelling. The page also notes that Avalon Airport is a different airport with different transfer options; confirm which airport is on the ticket.

section_heading: What happens after travelling without a valid ticket
text: A passenger must hold and use a valid ticket for the trip. If a myki is not tapped correctly, Transport Victoria says it may not be a valid ticket and a passenger may be fined. An authorised officer may report an alleged offence; the Department of Transport and Planning decides whether to issue a warning, infringement or take another action. Current fine amounts and review options should be checked on the official page, not inferred from an old example.

section_heading: Where a Victorian rental bond is held
text: The Residential Tenancies Bond Authority (RTBA) holds Victorian residential rental bonds in trust. When a renter pays the bond to a rental provider, the provider must lodge it with the RTBA within 14 days. The renter should review and accept the online lodgement, check that the names and amount are correct, and keep the bond receipt and number. A bond is not the same as rent paid in advance.

Victorian bonds are claimed through the RTBA website. A rental provider must start a claim within 14 days of the rental agreement ending unless a renter starts one first, and each renter then receives an email to review and accept it. Any renter whose name is on the bond can start a claim after the agreement ends, but must first authenticate their identity with Service Victoria. Once everyone has accepted a claim, the RTBA usually repays the bond within one business day.

section_heading: When a bond claim is disputed
text: Renters and rental providers are encouraged to negotiate an agreement about any deduction, for example when a renter believes damage is fair wear and tear. When a renter starts a claim, the RTBA must notify the other parties, who have 14 days to contest it by applying to VCAT or Rental Dispute Resolution Victoria (RDRV). If no one contests, the bond is repaid as claimed. If there is a dispute, VCAT or RDRV makes a legally binding order and the RTBA repays the bond in accordance with that order.

Before signing a Victorian rental agreement, read and keep a copy of the agreement and ask questions about unclear terms. At the start of the tenancy, the rental provider must give the renter a condition report and information including the provider or agent's contact details and an emergency contact number. Record the property's condition, return the report by the stated deadline and keep a copy with dated photographs. Check the current Consumer Affairs Victoria guidance for exact obligations.

section_heading: Urgent repairs in a rental property
text: Victorian urgent repairs include a blocked or broken toilet, gas leak, dangerous electrical fault, serious roof leak, or failure of an essential hot-water, water, cooking, heating or laundering service. Contact the rental provider or agent immediately using the emergency number provided at move-in and confirm the request in writing. The provider must arrange urgent repairs immediately. Keep records of contact attempts and receipts; continue paying rent while the repair is unresolved.

section_heading: If an urgent repair is not arranged
text: If the provider or agent does not respond promptly after being notified, a renter may organise and pay for an urgent repair costing $2,500 or less, then send written notice and receipts requesting repayment. The provider has seven days after receiving the notice to repay. For a repair over $2,500, do not arrange it yourself under this pathway; apply to Rental Dispute Resolution Victoria (RDRV) for help. The official page was last updated 26 February 2026.

Rent in advance is rent paid before the period it covers; it is a payment to the rental provider and is not money held as a bond. Victorian rules limit how much rent can usually be requested in advance, with exceptions such as rent above the statutory weekly threshold. The precise limit depends on the payment frequency and rent amount. Check the current Consumer Affairs Victoria page and keep a receipt showing which rental period the payment covers.

Study Melbourne describes private rentals, student accommodation, homestay and short-term stays as possible housing options. Availability, contract terms and costs differ. Students are advised to inspect accommodation before signing or paying where possible, read the agreement, understand what is included, and use official or reputable provider information. A homestay arrangement is not necessarily the same legal arrangement as a residential tenancy, so check the agreement and obtain advice if the terms are unclear.

Banks set their own identity and application requirements. Study Melbourne recommends checking the selected bank's current document list; students commonly need identity evidence such as a passport and may be asked for enrolment or address information. Some banks let a new arrival start the process before travelling, but identity verification may still be required in Australia. Compare fees and access arrangements, and never send identity documents through an unverified link.

section_heading: Applying for a tax file number
text: A tax file number (TFN) is a personal identifier used in the Australian tax and superannuation system. Eligible foreign passport holders and temporary visitors can apply online through the Australian Taxation Office's foreign-passport-holder process while in Australia, using the identity documents listed by the ATO. Applying for a TFN is free. Use the official ATO service rather than a paid intermediary, and do not share the TFN publicly because it is sensitive personal information.

An overseas student's tax residency is not decided by their visa alone; the ATO assesses it using residency tests such as the resides test. The ATO treats six months as a considerable time when deciding whether a person's behaviour is consistent with residing in Australia, but time alone is not decisive. Its guidance on people entering Australia specifically considers students studying here. If a person has recently arrived, the ATO's 'Are you a resident?' tool can help work out their residency status.

section_heading: Whether a tax return must be lodged
text: Whether a person must lodge a tax return depends on their circumstances for that income year. The ATO's 'Do I need to lodge a tax return?' tool works out whether a return is needed for income years from 2012-13 to 2025-26. If the result shows a return is not needed, the person must submit a non-lodgment advice, which is linked from the results page. Keep income statements and seek registered tax advice for complex cases.

section_heading: Declaring food at the Australian border
text: Food brought into Australia needs to be declared on the Incoming Passenger Card when arriving by plane, and certain items must be declared even in small amounts or as ingredients for cooking. Biosecurity officers may need to inspect some of the food. Australia has strict biosecurity procedures to prevent harmful pests and diseases from entering the country. Some items are allowed if restrictions are met, while others are not allowed or need permission, so check the Australian Border Force item list before packing. Do not assume that sealed or familiar food does not need to be declared.

Study Melbourne's pre-departure checklist recommends confirming that the student visa is approved, reviewing its conditions and accepting the offer letter from the education provider. Students should make sure their passport is valid for at least six months and keep printed and digital copies of key documents. The checklist also covers arranging OSHC and travel insurance, having enough funds for travel and early living costs, and carrying some cash or a card for immediate purchases. Before departure, confirm accommodation for arrival and transport from the airport, and tell the education provider the travel dates.

section_heading: Applying for a Victorian Proof of Age card
text: Service Victoria's steps for a Proof of Age card start with getting the application form from a VicRoads branch, an Australia Post branch or a selected pharmacy. The applicant needs two original identity documents and has the form and ID witnessed by a person they have known for at least one year who is enrolled to vote. The applicant also signs a declaration before an authorised person and has a photo taken at an approved photo location. The form is lodged with a $10 fee, and the card arrives in three to four weeks.

section_heading: Proving age and identity as a student
text: In Australia there is no legal requirement to carry identification, but proof of age may be needed to buy alcohol or enter some venues. Study Melbourne lists a proof of age card, an Australian driver licence or a passport as documents that can prove age. A Victorian proof of age card can be used anywhere in Australia, and Australia Post's Keypass card is also recognised as proof of age and identity. An overseas driver licence may be usable for driving if it is in English or translated into English.

Study Australia says Australian education providers offer a wide range of student support services, including on-arrival welcome and orientation programs, academic and student support advisers, language and learning support, and mental health, wellbeing and counselling services. Many providers also offer employment and careers services, childcare, clubs and societies, and student accommodation and housing services. Services and eligibility vary, so check the provider's website for current contacts. Use emergency services if there is immediate danger.

Condition 8202 requires a Student visa holder to remain enrolled in a registered course, maintain the required Australian Qualifications Framework level, and maintain satisfactory attendance and course progress as required by the education provider. A registered course is listed on CRICOS. The provider sets the applicable study-period expectations. Students concerned about attendance, progress or changing courses should contact the provider promptly and check their visa grant conditions; individual migration advice may be needed.

Call Triple Zero (000) if there is an emergency, immediate danger or a crime happening now. When answered, say whether police, fire or ambulance is needed, explain the exact location and follow the operator's instructions. Study Melbourne notes 112 may be dialled when outside mobile coverage or not connected to the network, and 106 is for people with a speech or hearing impairment. Do not delay an emergency call to search online.

section_heading: Free legal help through Study Melbourne
text: If an international student needs help understanding their rights or has a legal problem about employment or accommodation, the Study Melbourne Hub can advise where to get legal help. This may include online resources or a referral to the International Student Employment and Accommodation Legal Program (ISEALP) or other free community legal services. The advice is free, confidential and independent, and the Hub can be contacted on 1800 056 449. Examples include unpaid wages, unfair treatment at work, a bond that is not returned or a rent increase.

Each Australian state and territory offers free support services for international students, such as support officers, careers advice, counselling, social activities and legal advice. Education providers also offer academic and student support advisers and counselling services. A student who is having a hard time can talk to a counsellor at their place of study or to a GP. Use emergency services if there is immediate danger.
